name: Reported Speech
moduleIntroduction: Welcome to the Reported Speech module! This is the grammar of gossip and storytelling. In French, you often keep the original tense (*Il a dit qu'il est malade*). In English, if the main verb is past (*He said*), you usually push everything back into the past (*He said he was sick*). This is called 'Backshifting'.
contrastiveExplanation:
The Backstep (Tense Shift):
English: Present -> Past. Past -> Past Perfect. Will -> Would.
French: Often keeps the original tense.

Say vs. Tell:
English: Say (something). Tell (someone).
French: 'Dire' works for both. (Dire à quelqu'un -> Tell someone).

Indirect Questions:
English: Statement Order (Subject + Verb). No 'Do/Did'.
French: Il a demandé où j'habite. English: He asked where I lived.

commonErrors.wrong: He said me that he was busy.
commonErrors.correct: He told me that he was busy.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Direct translation of 'Il m'a dit'. 'Say' cannot take a person object without 'to'. Use 'Tell'.
French logic ('Il a dit qu'il viendra'). In English past narration, 'will' becomes 'would'.

commonErrors.wrong: He asked me where is the bank.
commonErrors.correct: He asked me where the bank was.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Keeping the question order. Reported questions must use statement order (Subject + Verb).

commonErrors.wrong: She told that she was tired.
commonErrors.correct: She said that she was tired.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Using 'Tell' without a listener. 'Tell' requires an object (Tell *someone*).

commonErrors.wrong: He said he bought the car.
commonErrors.correct: He said he had bought the car.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Not shifting the Past Simple back. If he bought it *before* he said it, use Past Perfect.

items.questionText: "I am happy." -> He said he ___ happy.
"I like football." -> He said he ___ football.
"I will help you." -> She said she ___ help me.
"I can swim." -> He said he ___ swim.
He ___ me that he was tired.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Told' is followed by a person (me).

items.questionText: She ___ that she was hungry.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Said' is used without a person object.

items.questionText: "I am working." -> He said he ___ working.
"I don't know." -> He said he ___ know.
"My car is blue." -> He said ___ car was blue.
items.feedback: Correct! Pronoun shift: My -> His (if speaker is male).

items.questionText: "I have a dog." -> She said she ___ a dog.
"It isn't raining." -> He said it ___ raining.
He told ___ a story.
"We are late." -> They said ___ were late.
"I must go." -> He said he ___ go.
"I am going." -> She said she ___ going.
"It is cold." -> He said it ___ cold.
She ___ to him.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Said' can take 'to + person'. (Told him / Said to him).

items.questionText: "I feel sick." -> He said he ___ sick.
"You are nice." -> He told me I ___ nice.
"I play piano." -> She said she ___ piano.
"I saw him." -> He said he ___ him.
items.feedback: Correct! Past Simple (saw) shifts to Past Perfect (had seen).

items.questionText: "Where do you live?" -> He asked me where I ___.
items.feedback: Correct! Question order changes to Statement order (Subject + Verb). Tense shifts.

items.questionText: "I have eaten." -> She said she ___ eaten.
items.feedback: Correct! Present Perfect (have eaten) -> Past Perfect (had eaten).

items.questionText: "I am coming tomorrow." -> He said he was coming ___.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Tomorrow' changes to 'the next day' or 'the following day'.

items.questionText: "Are you happy?" -> He asked if I ___ happy.
items.feedback: Correct! Yes/No question uses 'If' + Statement order.

items.questionText: "I visited Kribi last year." -> He said he had visited Kribi ___.
"Don't speak!" -> The teacher told us ___ speak.
"I will see you here." -> He said he would see me ___.
"Do you like coffee?" -> She asked me ___ I liked coffee.
"We must study." -> He said they ___ study.
"Sit down." -> He told me ___ down.
"What time is it?" -> He asked what time ___.
"I may be late." -> She said she ___ be late.
"I can help." -> He said he ___ help.
"I have been waiting." -> He said he ___ waiting.
items.feedback: Correct! Present Perfect Continuous -> Past Perfect Continuous.

items.questionText: "Why are you crying?" -> He asked me why I ___.
"This is my book." -> He said ___ was his book.
"I will call you tonight." -> He said he would call me ___.
"Please help me." -> She ___ me to help her.
"Who broke the window?" -> He asked who ___ the window.
"I should have gone." -> He said he ___ gone.
items.feedback: Correct! Modals like 'should', 'could', 'would' do NOT change.

items.questionText: "Let's go to the cinema." -> He ___ going to the cinema.
"If I were you, I would go." -> He ___ me to go.
"I didn't do it!" -> He ___ doing it.
He suggested ___ a taxi.
"Water boils at 100 degrees." -> He said water ___ at 100 degrees.
items.feedback: Correct! Universal truths do NOT need to change tense.

items.questionText: "Don't forget to call." -> He ___ me to call.
"I am sorry I was late." -> He apologized for ___ late.
"Why don't we go out?" -> He suggested ___ out.
"You stole the money!" -> He accused me ___ stealing the money.
Find the error: "He suggested me to go."
items.feedback: Correct! 'Suggest' cannot be followed by 'Person + to'. Say 'Suggested that I go' or 'Suggested going'.

items.questionText: "I'll pay." -> He insisted on ___.
"If I were rich, I would travel." -> He said if he ___ rich, he would travel.
items.feedback: Correct! Second Conditional (Unreal) usually doesn't change in reported speech.

items.questionText: "I used to live here." -> He said he ___ to live there.
He asked me what ___ doing.
"I wish I knew." -> He said he wished he ___.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Wish' + Past usually stays the same (or changes to Past Perfect, but 'knew' is acceptable/common). Actually, strictly, past simple in wish clauses often remains.

items.questionText: "No, I won't go." -> He refused ___.
"I bought the car." -> She confirmed that she ___ the car.
"Congratulations on passing." -> He congratulated me ___ passing.
Find the error: "He told that he was busy."
items.feedback: Correct! 'Told' must be followed by a person. Use 'said' or 'told me'.

items.questionText: "I am tired." -> She said she ___ tired.
"I want water." -> He said he ___ water.
"I will call." -> He said he ___ call.
"I can drive." -> She said she ___ drive.
He ___ me a lie.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Told' + person. Also fixed phrase 'Tell a lie'.

items.questionText: "I will help." -> He insisted on ___.
